name: Himeji Castle (White Heron Castle)
description: Japan's most spectacular and best-preserved feudal samurai castle, renowned for its brilliant white plastered wooden walls.
history: Masterpiece of defensive castle architecture that survived the Meiji restoration, World War II bombings, and major earthquakes without damage.
construction: Built on a hill with high curving stone walls (Musha-gaeshi), 83 rooms, and intricate spiral maze defenses.
architecture: Six-story wooden keep with fireproof white plaster, projecting gables, and gun-slit arrow loops.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1993; Japan's premier national treasure.
currentStatus: Standing pristine in Himeji, Hyogo Prefecture, Japan.
